title: Derived direct image commutes with restriction to opens
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] (more generally of ringed spaces). Let $V\subseteq Y$ be open, put $U=f^{-1}(V)$ and let $g:U\to V$ be the induced morphism. Then for every $E$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] there is a canonical isomorphism $(Rf_*E)|_V\cong Rg_*(E|_U)$ in $D(\mathcal O_V)$, natural in $E$, with $Rf_*$, $Rg_*$ the derived direct images [def-pc-derived-direct-image].

source.place: Lemma lemma-restrict-direct-image-open (Tag 08FE), line 7901; proof via Lemma 08BS (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open)

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution E \to I^\bullet on X. Since U=f^{-1}(V) is open in X, [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open] says that I^\bullet|_U is K-injective on U, so it computes Rg_*(E|_U).

source.place: Lemma 08BS, used in the proof of Lemma 08FE

proof.text: By the K-injective construction of derived direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], Rf_*E is represented by f_*I^\bullet and Rg_*(E|_U) by g_*(I^\bullet|_U). For every open W\subseteq V, (g_*I^\bullet|_U)(W)=I^\bullet(f^{-1}(W))=(f_*I^\bullet)(W), so these complexes are canonically identical after restricting f_*I^\bullet to V. The componentwise identifications commute with differentials and are natural in E, giving the canonical derived isomorphism.
